name: pass1-domain-binding
description: Dimension 7 (Domain Binding) against a two-page domain-reference kit (fictional marina-berthing domain) plus its Go slice. The prompt passes ONLY the glossary page's path — the traps counterpart must be auto-discovered by the sibling naming convention and the pair reviewed as one composite artifact. The kit's binding claims discriminate every dimension-7 verdict: three terms and the L1 enforcement pointer verify; the Dockage Rate binding names a symbol absent from an existing file (violated); the Waitlist Entry binding cites a file absent from the tree (dangling-anchor — the harness stages the whole test-files/ tree, so the absence of berths/waitlist.go is an observable fixture property; files[] cannot express absence); Haul-Out is a future term with 'Bindings: none yet' (internally-sound); Transient Stay is a future binding naming no code-element kind (ill-formed negative control). L3 additionally carries the fabricated-labeled+settled provenance branch (explicitly invented placeholder presented as 'canonical — settled harbor policy') for Pass 2 Check C. `oracle/expected-verdicts.json` is the grader-only oracle — outside `test-files/`, never staged as skill input.
prompt: Review the domain-reference kit at marina.md.
trap: The reviewer is likely to (a) fail the composite acceptance — review the glossary solo, demand the traps page's path, or reject the kit as a non-architecture artifact; (b) route binding claims to `unrouted` (honoring the old do-not-force-fit rule against a dimension set that stopped at 6) or force-fit them into dimensions 1–2; (c) blur the violated/dangling-anchor seam — grade the missing RateSchedule symbol `dangling-anchor` (the cited file exists; the element inside it is what is missing) or grade the missing berths/waitlist.go `violated` (the anchor itself is absent); (d) excuse the Waitlist Entry binding as greenfield/future although its term is present-tense; (e) grade Haul-Out's 'Bindings: none yet' against the repo and emit a finding for a claim that says outright nothing is built; (f) cross the altitude line by truth-verifying rule intent or term definitions against code behavior; or (g) miss the fabricated-labeled L3 presented as settled (Check C P2) while over-firing on the correctly-`proposed` reverse-engineered rules L1/L2.

assertions.text: Composite acceptance: from the single glossary path (marina.md), the counterpart marina-traps.md is auto-discovered via the sibling naming convention and the pair is reviewed as ONE composite artifact — no rejection, no request for a second path, no solo-page note.
Every per-term Bindings claim and the L1 enforcement pointer are routed to dimension 7 (numeric token 7) in the Claim Set. NO binding claim lands `unrouted` or is force-fit into dimensions 1–6.

Rule intent is not truth-verified: L1/L2/L3's intent (what the business means the rule to be) receives no topology verdict against the repo — only their enforcement pointers are graded, and the intent claims surface provenance-labeled (routed `pass2`/`unrouted` and handled by Pass 2), per the mining-table kit row.

The Berth, Mooring Assignment, and Vessel bindings and the L1 enforcement pointer (`hasActiveAssignment` in moorings/assign.go) are each graded `verified` in reality mode, with evidence naming the inspected file(s).
The Dockage Rate binding is graded `violated` (P1): berths/registry.go exists but declares no `RateSchedule` symbol — a missing element inside an existing anchor. It is NOT graded `dangling-anchor`.

The Waitlist Entry binding is graded `dangling-anchor` (P2): the cited file berths/waitlist.go does not exist in the tree. It is NOT graded `violated` and NOT excused as greenfield/future (the term is present-tense).
Haul-Out ('Bindings: none yet', future wording) is graded `internally-sound` in internal-soundness mode — it is NOT graded against the repo and draws no finding.
Transient Stay ('will be represented in code' — no code-element kind, no location class) is graded `ill-formed` (P2) as the fallback-arm negative control.

L2's enforcement pointer ('see traps D1') is resolved against the counterpart page and found present — the pointer resolves, the documented divergence is NOT re-reported as a new finding, and no `ill-formed` is emitted for it.

Pass 2 Check C fires for L3: a P2 self-certification finding in the Provenance subsection, quoting the settled presentation ('canonical — settled harbor policy') and the invented-placeholder marker, and noting no ratification source is cited.
Over-fire controls: no provenance finding for L1/L2 (reverse-engineered but correctly `proposed`) and no finding against the kit's `proposed` term entries or freshness banners.
Severity mapping: the Dockage Rate `violated` is P1; the Waitlist Entry `dangling-anchor` and the Transient Stay `ill-formed` are P2 — per the output contract.
